scope: Primary citation locators, source-specific support limits and additional corroborating references; no changes to verdicts, eligibility or timing judgments.

sources.title: Apple introduces iPod shuffle (2005)
sources.provenance_note: Documents a USB flash-storage music player and immediate shipping. Flash storage supports an absence of mechanical storage, not the absence of all physical switches.
sources.access_note: Primary page examined for this dated citation supplement. Outcome cutoff remains 2026-10-15.

sources.title: Apple reinvents the phone with iPhone
sources.provenance_note: Documents the soft keyboard, Multi-Touch interface, EDGE/Wi-Fi and pocketable device. January was an announcement with US availability planned for June 2007; it is not a January retail launch.
sources.access_note: Primary page examined for this dated citation supplement. Outcome cutoff remains 2026-10-15.

sources.title: Microsoft unveils Windows Home Server at CES 2007
sources.provenance_note: A forward-looking announcement of a home-local server architecture. Establishes design and announced functions, not sales, adoption or contemporaneous retail availability.
sources.access_note: Primary page examined for this dated citation supplement. Outcome cutoff remains 2026-10-15.

sources.title: Windows Home Server — Microsoft Lifecycle
sources.provenance_note: Official product lifecycle starts 2007-10-11. This is a product-support date, not a household-adoption measure; the webpage publication date is not given.
sources.access_note: Primary page examined for this dated citation supplement. Outcome cutoff remains 2026-10-15.

sources.title: Apple updates MacBook family (October 2008)
sources.provenance_note: The MacBook Air update explicitly states three pounds and a 0.16–0.76-inch enclosure. This is evidence by October 2008, not a claimed first-ever lightweight notebook.
sources.access_note: Primary page examined for this dated citation supplement. Outcome cutoff remains 2026-10-15.

citations.locator: Product-feature bullets: notebook weight with battery, and with DVD drive.
citations.finding: The manufacturer lists 5.7 lb with a weight-saving module and 6.1 lb with the DVD drive.
citations.limitations: Configuration-specific comparison, not a market-wide average.

citations.locator: Opening product description; storage-options paragraph.
citations.finding: The launch announcement specifies 0.16–0.76-inch thickness and describes hard-disk and optional SSD configurations.
citations.limitations: This page does not give a three-pound weight; the added October 2008 source supplies that specification.

citations.locator: Opening product description and thickness/weight feature bullets.
citations.finding: Apple specifies a one-inch enclosure and 5.3 lb including battery and DVD drive.
citations.limitations: A named model is a comparator, not proof of every notebook’s specifications.

citations.locator: Opening announcement and descriptions of wireless application downloads and Multi-Touch features.
citations.finding: The release establishes downloadable applications on iPhone/iPod touch and their touch interface.
citations.limitations: It does not establish storage technology or the absence of moving components; see the added flash-player source.

citations.locator: Multi-Touch feature paragraph and cellular/Wi-Fi application-delivery paragraphs.
citations.finding: This documents touch-based software use on the supported devices.
citations.limitations: It does not quantify the share of keyboard-free portable computers; the added original iPhone announcement directly describes a soft keyboard.

citations.locator: Opening sales paragraph and descriptions of digital movie distribution.
citations.finding: The release documents billions of digital song downloads and a substantial movie-download business.
citations.limitations: This is digital-collection context only, not evidence of home-server ownership or the adoption denominator.

citations.locator: Wireless-delivery section and Books, Blogs, Magazines and Newspapers section.
citations.finding: The 2007 Kindle release describes EVDO delivery of books and periodicals without a computer or Wi-Fi hotspot.
citations.limitations: This establishes available functions; it does not establish the share of all media delivered wirelessly.

citations.locator: Opening sales paragraph and catalogue descriptions.
citations.finding: Apple reports five billion song downloads and more than 50,000 daily movie rentals/purchases by June 2008.
citations.limitations: These are digital-distribution counts, not wireless-only transactions or all-media market share.

citations.locator: Wireless-download paragraph and cellular/Wi-Fi distribution paragraph.
citations.finding: The July 2008 release explicitly describes direct app downloads over cellular networks and Wi-Fi.
citations.limitations: The same release also describes USB syncing; wireless availability does not mean cables had disappeared.

citations.locator: Opening Bluetooth product description and cable-replacement feature paragraphs.
citations.finding: Apple introduced Bluetooth keyboards and mice in September 2003, directly supporting peripheral cable substitution.
citations.limitations: The release does not show that monitor cables or power leads were eliminated.

citations.locator: Paragraph describing cellular-network and Wi-Fi access to the App Store.
citations.finding: The release confirms operational wireless software delivery on shipping mobile platforms.
citations.limitations: It does not measure continuous coverage, throughput or population-wide usage.

citations.locator: Reads Like Paper section; Books, Blogs, Magazines and Newspapers section.
citations.finding: Amazon describes a reflective electronic-paper screen and wireless access to books and periodicals in 2007.
citations.limitations: The display description is a manufacturer claim, not an independent equivalence test against paper.

citations.locator: Opening notebook description and hardware/features paragraphs.
citations.finding: The announcement documents an unusually thin notebook and built-in wireless features.
citations.limitations: It is one full-sized notebook, not evidence for the full range of tiny computing form factors.

citations.locator: Opening product description and Holds Hundreds of Books in 10.3 Ounces section.
citations.finding: The 2007 Kindle is a small electronic-reading form factor with wireless access and local storage.
citations.limitations: Its listed functions and size do not make it a general-purpose keyboard-free computer.

citations.locator: Opening iPhone/iPod touch description and native-application availability paragraph.
citations.finding: The release documents a programmable mobile-device application ecosystem before 2009.
citations.limitations: This citation establishes available applications, not physical dimensions or every proposed form factor.

citations.locator: Wireless Internet Use overview: opening wireless-use finding and mobile-use comparison bullets.
citations.finding: Pew reports 56% of Americans had ever used wireless Internet and 19% used mobile Internet the previous day in its April 2009 survey.
citations.limitations: These are US adult survey measures, not global population coverage, wireless traffic share or a continuous-service guarantee.

citations.locator: USB flash-drive paragraph and Pricing & Availability section.
citations.finding: Apple documents a shipping flash-storage player in January 2005. Interpreting flash storage as avoiding mechanical disk storage supports the portable-device criterion.
citations.limitations: This is an editorial inference about storage; physical switches remain, and the source does not establish a majority across all personal devices.

citations.locator: iPhone is a Revolutionary Mobile Phone section: SMS and touch-keyboard paragraph.
citations.finding: The original iPhone announcement explicitly describes an onscreen keyboard, directly supporting the availability of physical-keyboard-free portables.
citations.limitations: The announcement is not a device-population share study and does not establish majority adoption in 2009.

citations.locator: Data-networking paragraph and Breakthrough Internet Communications Device section.
citations.finding: Apple describes EDGE and Wi-Fi web/email access on the announced 2007 iPhone.
citations.limitations: This documents product capability, not reliable universal coverage or usage prevalence.

citations.locator: Simplifying Digital Life and Connecting Digital Devices and Experiences sections.
citations.finding: Microsoft describes automatic PC backups, centralized home media and remote Internet access from a home-local server.
citations.limitations: This adds direct architecture evidence. The January announcement projected release later in 2007 and supplies no evidence that most households adopted it.

citations.locator: Support Dates table: Windows Home Server start date.
citations.finding: The official lifecycle entry gives 2007-10-11 as the product start date, corroborating a pre-2009 product timeline.
citations.limitations: A support start date is not a retail shipment count or evidence of widespread home-server ownership.

citations.locator: Paragraph announcing updates to MacBook Air and the 17-inch MacBook Pro.
citations.finding: The October 2008 release explicitly specifies a three-pound MacBook Air and a maximum enclosure height of 0.76 inches.
citations.limitations: This confirms the weight missing from the January release; it does not establish an exact first-achievement date.

citations.locator: Opening wearable-device description and USB flash-drive paragraph.
citations.finding: The shipping player demonstrates a small wearable digital device with flash storage and computer connectivity.
citations.limitations: A music player is not a substitute for every general-purpose-computer form factor in the forecast.

citations.locator: Opening product description and Pricing & Availability section.
citations.finding: The 2007 announcement describes a small handheld combining phone, media player and Internet functions.
citations.limitations: The source documents a planned product and functions, not universality or the success of every miniature form factor.
